title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
technique: chunked prefills + stall-free batching with a token budget derived from the TBT SLO

optimized_metrics.evidence: we use a throughput metric, Capacity, defined as the maximum request load (queries-per-second) a system can sustain while meeting certain latency targets. Higher capacity is desirable because it reduces the cost of serving.
we define the SLO on P99 TBT to be equal to 5x and 25x the execution time of a decode iteration for a request (with prefill length of 4k and 32 batch size) running without any prefill interference
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: we define the SLO on P99 TBT to be equal to 5x and 25x the execution time of a decode iteration; We focus on ... the 99th percentile (P99) for TBT values

optimized_metrics.evidence: Stall-free scheduling unlocks the opportunity to improve throughput with large batch sizes while minimizing the effect of batching on latency.
this allows us to create balanced micro-batching based schedules that significantly reduce pipeline bubbles and improve GPU utilization

headline_claim.text: For Mistral-7B on single A100 GPUs, we achieve 2.6x higher serving capacity and up to 3.7x higher serving capacity for the Yi-34B model on two A100 GPUs as compared to vLLM. When used with pipeline parallelism on Falcon-180B, Sarathi-Serve provides up to 5.6x gain in the end-to-end serving capacity.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For a given request, TTFT measures the latency of generating the first output token from the moment a request arrives in the system.
TBT on the other hand measures the interval between the generation of consecutive output tokens of a request, and affects the overall perceived fluidity of the response.
metric_definitions.notes: token-level distribution; P99 over all decode tokens

metric_definitions.definition_quote: a throughput metric, Capacity, defined as the maximum request load (queries-per-second) a system can sustain while meeting certain latency targets.
metric_definitions.notes: max sustainable QPS under P99-TBT SLO (and sustainability: median scheduling delay <= 2 s); not SLO-attainment-fraction-based

metric_definitions.definition_quote: prefill-prioritizing schedulers lead to an undesirable phenomenon that we refer to as generation stalls
metric_definitions.notes: ongoing decodes paused by a long prefill; shows up as TBT spikes of several seconds

slo_spec: P99 TBT SLO = 5x (strict) or 25x (relaxed) the decode-iteration time (prefill len 4k, batch 32, no prefill interference), following Patel et al.; Table 3 absolute values: Mistral-7B 0.1/0.5 s, Yi-34B 0.2/1 s, LLaMA2-70B 1/5 s, Falcon-180B 1/5 s (strict/relaxed). Sustainability: median scheduling delay <= 2 s.
load_regime: Poisson arrival request-rate sweep to find max capacity; datasets openchat_sharegpt4 and arxiv_summarization
tradeoff_acknowledged: explicitly a throughput-latency tradeoff: prefill-prioritizing (vLLM/Orca) gets throughput at cost of high TBT tail; decode-prioritizing (FasterTransformer) low TBT but low throughput; smaller token budget reduces TBT but increases chunking overhead
extractor_notes: Metrics paragraph: 'We focus on the median value for the TTFT ... and on the 99th percentile (P99) for TBT'. The SLO is only on TBT; TTFT is reported but not constrained. Capacity is a max-QPS-under-SLO number (goodput-like) rather than a goodput fraction. Token budget is derived from the TBT SLO (Algorithm 3).
load_class_quote: The request arrival times are generated using Poisson distribution (§5.1); capacity = maximum request load (queries-per-second) a system can sustain while meeting certain latency targets (§2.4)
